reference.source: Comprehensive Clinical Nephrology / Oxford Textbook of Medicine
clinicalPearls: A recessive ciliopathy from PKHD1 mutations affecting fibrocystin, presenting in the fetus, newborn or young child
The kidneys show diffuse fusiform dilatation of the collecting ducts, appearing as large, echogenic kidneys with poor corticomedullary differentiation on ultrasound
It is characteristically paired with congenital hepatic fibrosis, so hepatobiliary disease and portal hypertension are integral to the phenotype, not incidental
Severely affected neonates may have oligohydramnios, pulmonary hypoplasia and the Potter sequence, and respiratory failure is a leading early cause of death
Surviving children commonly develop systemic hypertension, progressive chronic kidney disease and complications of portal hypertension such as varices and hypersplenism
Diagnosis rests on characteristic renal and hepatic imaging in a child of consanguineous or affected-sibling background, supported by PKHD1 genetic testing
Care is multidisciplinary, combining blood-pressure control, management of kidney failure, and surveillance and treatment of portal hypertension and cholangitis
reference.pathophysiology: ARPKD results from biallelic mutations in PKHD1, encoding fibrocystin (polyductin), a protein of the primary cilium and basal body of renal and biliary epithelium. Defective fibrocystin disrupts normal tubular and ductal development, producing non-obstructive fusiform dilatation of the renal collecting ducts and abnormal remodelling of the biliary tree (ductal plate malformation) with congenital hepatic fibrosis. Massive kidney enlargement in utero can restrict lung growth and amniotic fluid, while progressive tubular and interstitial injury impairs renal concentrating ability and glomerular filtration, and hepatic fibrosis leads to portal hypertension.
additionalDifferentials: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease presenting in childhood
Congenital hepatic fibrosis from other causes
additionalInvestigations: Renal ultrasound showing enlarged echogenic kidneys with loss of corticomedullary differentiation
Hepatic imaging for biliary ductal ectasia, hepatic fibrosis and splenomegaly
Serial blood pressure measurement and renal function monitoring
Prenatal ultrasound for kidney size and amniotic fluid volume where relevant
Assessment for portal hypertension including platelet count and varices surveillance
PKHD1 genetic testing and parental carrier assessment
redFlags: Neonatal respiratory distress from pulmonary hypoplasia
Severe or poorly controlled hypertension in an infant or child
Variceal bleeding or features of decompensated portal hypertension
Ascending cholangitis with fever and sepsis
reference.prognosis: Outcome depends heavily on surviving the neonatal period, since perinatal respiratory failure is a major early risk; children who survive infancy can live into adulthood but face progressive kidney failure and complications of congenital hepatic fibrosis requiring lifelong specialist care.
pitfalls: Overlooking the hepatobiliary disease, which drives much of the long-term morbidity
Assuming absence of a family history excludes a recessive disorder
Underestimating hypertension severity in young children
Failing to arrange surveillance for portal hypertension and cholangitis
management: In severely affected newborns the immediate priority is respiratory support for pulmonary hypoplasia, including mechanical ventilation
Control the frequently severe systemic hypertension with renin-angiotensin system blockade using an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin-receptor blocker
Manage progressive chronic kidney disease with attention to nutrition and growth, correction of anaemia and mineral-and-bone disorder, and salt and water balance
Address congenital hepatic fibrosis and portal hypertension through varices surveillance and banding, management of hypersplenism, and prompt antibiotics for cholangitis
Monitor blood pressure, renal and hepatic function and growth at regular intervals
Plan renal replacement therapy and transplantation, considering combined liver-kidney transplantation where hepatic disease is severe
Provide genetic counselling and carrier testing for the family, noting autosomal recessive inheritance and consanguinity
